text.en:
Class 6 had to choose a monitor. Each candidate told the class what they would do. Everyone voted with a slip of paper and the one with the most votes became monitor.
"This is how our country chooses leaders too," said the teacher.

Governance means managing a community, village, city or country: making rules, providing services such as water, roads, schools and hospitals, and keeping people safe.
In a democracy, the people have the power to choose who will govern them. India is the largest democracy in the world.
Citizens aged 18 and above can vote. They elect representatives in elections by secret ballot. The representatives make decisions for everyone and must answer to the people.
Governance in India works at three levels: local (village and town), state and national (the Union).
Local governance is closest to people. It deals with daily needs such as clean water, streets, lights and rubbish.
Governance means running a place: making rules and giving services like water, roads and schools.
In a democracy, people choose their government through elections.
Every citizen aged eighteen or more can vote. The vote is secret.
Governance has three levels: local, state and national. Local governance is closest to us.

problem.en: Why is a secret ballot important in an election?

text.en: In a secret ballot, no one knows whom you voted for.

why.en: It hides your choice from others.

text.en: So nobody can force or pressure you.

prompt.en: A friend says his vote does not matter because there are millions of voters. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Every vote counts, and many votes together decide the result.
Voting is how citizens choose who governs them.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking one vote has no value.

points.en: Governance means managing a place and its services.
In a democracy people choose representatives by voting.
There are local, state and national levels.
